newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen advancing moderately.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen advancing moderately.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to make a moderate advance on Thursday with further buying of blue-chip issues after the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" business survey released on Wednesday fell within most participants' expectations, brokers said.
On Wednesday, the key Nikkei 225 average ended down 72.97 points or 0.34 percent at 21,345.28. Its December futures were down 40 points at 21,320.
"Since the "tankan" was in line with our expectations, the trend of buying blue-chips will not change for a while," said an analyst at a major Japanese securities house.
The tankan showed a slight improvement in business sentiment in Japan, with the key diffusion index for big manufacturers at minus 3 in November against minus 7 in the previous survey in August.
This meant that participants picturing gradual economic recovery would not need to change their scenarios, brokers said.

Analysts said that the Nikkei average would eventually head towards 21,612, a high marked on October 18. Some said they were focusing on whether it would close above 21,420, which would be a bullish sign in technical charts.
Losing issues overwhelmed gainers 830 to 185, while 189 issues were unchanged.
Declining sectors were led by sea transport, construction, mining, real estate and air transport. There were no major advancing sectors.
Profit-taking hit Honda Motor Co Ltd's shares in the morning, falling 110 to 3,360 yen. The auto maker's shares hit a record high on Wednesday.
Honda was the most actively traded stock in the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, with its volume increasing to 4.252 million shares.
